title: Can House Plants REALLY Purify the Air in Your Home?
description:
Indoor air pollution is a major concern, especially in cities like Delhi during Diwali, where stubble burning, crackers, and vehicular emissions choke the air. Many articles and YouTube channels claim that indoor plants like snake plant, aloe vera, peace lily, and tulsi can improve air quality. But what does science really say? Can houseplants actually clean the air in your home or office?

This video dives deep into the famous NASA Clean Air Study (1989), which is often cited as proof that indoor plants can purify air. We unpack what the study really tested, why it was designed for space station chambers and not living rooms, and why later studies show that you would need hundreds of plants per square metre to see any real benefit. We also explore volatile organic compounds (VOCs) like formaldehyde, benzene, and toluene that come from paints, furniture, and cleaners—and explain why plants alone cannot keep your indoor air safe.

If you’ve searched for “indoor plants air purifier, do plants clean air, NASA plant study, best indoor plants for pollution, snake plant air quality”, then this video will give you the scientific perspective. Don’t fall for myths spread by lifestyle blogs and viral reels—learn what peer-reviewed studies actually conclude.

Indoor plants are wonderful for decoration and mental health, but when it comes to purifying air, ventilation, air purifiers, and reducing VOC sources are far more effective solutions. Pale Blue Thoughts is here to clear the air—literally and figuratively. Don’t forget to like, comment, share, and subscribe if you enjoy myth-busting content backed by science.
